sentences.en: Today, we are diving into a topic that is pretty emotionally charged.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要深入探讨一个充满情感张力的话题。

sentences.en: It's definitely one of those areas of psychology and just growing up in existence that definitely hits close to home for a lot of people,
sentences.zh: 这绝对是心理学和成长经历中，让许多人感同身受的一个领域，

sentences.en: which is exactly why I think we're talking about it.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么我认为我们应该谈论它。

sentences.en: And what we're unpacking today is the psychology of emotionally immature parents.
sentences.zh: 我们今天要剖析的是情绪不成熟父母的心理学。

sentences.en: What kind of people they are, what it means, what it looks like, how it impacts us, and most importantly, how we can really move forward
sentences.zh: 他们是什麽样的人，这意味着什麽，表现如何，它们如何影响我们，以及最重要的是，我们如何才能真正向前看，

sentences.en: from a place of grace instead of frustration and needing to change them and wanting them to be different people.
sentences.zh: 以一种宽容的心态，而不是充满挫折感，去试图改变他们或希望他们成为不同的人。

sentences.en: Because as we will kind of illuminate through this episode, sometimes it's really, really difficult.
sentences.zh: 因为正如我们在本期节目中所阐明的，有时这真的非常非常难。

sentences.en: This is obviously a very sensitive subject for many of us.
sentences.zh: 对我们许多人来说，这显然是一个非常敏感的主题。

sentences.en: I think we often grow up thinking our parents can do no wrong.
sentences.zh: 我想我们常常在成长过程中认为父母永远不会犯错。

sentences.en: But as we gain, I guess, more independence, more knowledge, more self-awareness,
sentences.zh: 但随着我们获得更多的独立性、更多的知识、更多的自我意识，

sentences.en: cracks can really start to show.
sentences.zh: 裂痕确实开始显现。

sentences.en: And that can be so unnerving to unpack, especially because, you know, our parents are such prominent figures in our lives.
sentences.zh: 剖析这些会让人感到非常不安，特别是，你知道的，我们的父母在我们生活中扮演着如此突出的角色。

sentences.en: Our survival is so based on them for so long.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里，我们的生存极其依赖他们。

sentences.en: They are so important to us.
sentences.zh: 他们对我们太重要了。

sentences.en: So when we suddenly or slowly become aware of the ways in which they are flawed and the ways in which they have perhaps not showed up for us the way they needed to
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们突然或慢慢地意识到他们身上的瑕疵，意识到他们可能没有以我们需要的方式，

sentences.en: or should have been required to, it can be a bit of a epiphany aha moment followed by a real kind of crash and a real come down.
sentences.zh: 或者本应要求的方式陪伴我们时，这可能会带来一种顿悟式的“啊哈”时刻，随后伴随着真正的崩溃和严重的失落感。

sentences.en: You know, perhaps you have always sensed that something was off in your relationship with your parents.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许你一直隐约感觉到你和父母的关系有点不对劲。

sentences.en: You know, maybe they were loving but only on their terms or they were very present physically but very emotionally unavailable or they confided in you too much.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许他们充满爱意，但只限于他们的条件，或者他们在身体上非常在场，但在情感上却极度疏离，或者他们向你倾诉太多。

sentences.en: They leaned on you too heavily.
sentences.zh: 他们过分依赖你。

sentences.en: They made you feel like you had to be the adult in the relationship.
sentences.zh: 他们让你觉得你必须成为这段关系中的成年人。

sentences.en: And at the age you are now, you're kind of realizing, wait, other people's parents weren't like that.
sentences.zh: 以你现在的年龄，你开始意识到，等等，别人的父母不是这样的。

sentences.en: And maybe this has done some long-term damage to me.
sentences.zh: 也许这对我造成了一些长期的伤害。

sentences.en: And if any of that rings true, this episode is especially for you.
sentences.zh: 如果这些话触动了你的心弦，这一期节目就是特意为你准备的。

sentences.en: We're going to be exploring what emotional immaturity looks like, where it comes from psychologically, how it affects us in our 20s, and really importantly,
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨情绪不成熟是什么样子的，它在心理上从何而来，它如何影响我们二十多岁的生活，以及非常重要的一点，

sentences.en: how we can begin to heal, how we can break generational cycles.
sentences.zh: 我们如何开始疗愈，如何打破代际循环。

sentences.en: I also want to mention, I think it's important to say, this isn't going to be like a parent bashing episode.
sentences.zh: 我还想提一下，我认为有必要说明的是，这不会是一期声讨父母的节目。

sentences.en: I don't think that the right approach to this topic is blame.

sentences.en: I don't think that's helpful.

sentences.zh: 我们要做的，实际上是对寻找清晰度做出真诚的尝试，更好地理解这类人，并理解他们为什么会成为这样的人，

sentences.zh: 不是为了让他们有借口继续做那种人，继续影响和冲击我们的生活，而是为了让我们能够真正疗愈。

sentences.en: This is about us.

sentences.en: And you know, it is going to be different for every person.

sentences.en: There's some parts of this that you might not relate to, but I definitely hope that you can just feel a little bit less alone.

sentences.en: This kind of emotional immaturity that we're going to discuss, it often flies under the radar because it doesn't always look like overt or obvious trauma.

sentences.en: I know the word trauma really rings alarm bells, but these things, these experiences of being emotionally neglected or emotionally mistreated or even just psychologically confused

sentences.en: What do we really mean by emotionally immature parents?
sentences.zh: 我们所说的“情绪不成熟的父母”到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: Because it does seem kind of subjective in a way.
sentences.zh: 因为从某种程度上看，这似乎有点主观。

sentences.en: Well, the first thing you need to know is that this phrase was first popularized by Dr. Lindsay C.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你需要知道的第一件事是，这个词最初是由琳赛·C·吉布森

sentences.en: Gibson.
sentences.zh: 博士普及的。

sentences.en: She is a clinical psychologist and if you have ever even dipped your toe into this space before, you will probably know of her book,
sentences.zh: 她是一位临床心理学家，如果你曾经涉足过这个领域，你大概会知道她的书，

sentences.en: Adult Children of Emotionally Immature Parents.
sentences.zh: 《成年情绪不成熟父母的孩子》。

sentences.en: It was released in 2015.
sentences.zh: 它于2015年出版。

sentences.en: It is like the Bible on this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 这就像是该领域的圣经。

sentences.en: In this book, she basically introduces us to this idea of emotional immaturity as a set of traits that includes things like poor empathy, volatility,
sentences.zh: 在这本书中，她向我们介绍了情绪不成熟的概念，将其视为一组特征，包括同理心差、情绪多变、

sentences.en: self-centeredness and a real ingrained avoidance of emotional responsibility.
sentences.zh: 自我中心以及根深蒂固地逃避情感责任。

sentences.en: So what does this look like?
sentences.zh: 那么这具体是什么样子的呢？

sentences.en: This might look like parents who struggle to validate your emotions.
sentences.zh: 这可能表现为父母难以确认你的情绪。

sentences.en: So you've said you're anxious or you're frustrated or you're hurting and they said to calm down or they said that you were overreacting.
sentences.zh: 所以当你表达自己感到焦虑、沮丧或受伤时，他们会叫你冷静点，或者说你反应过度了。

sentences.en: Perhaps they took your requests or your feedback too personally.
sentences.zh: 也许他们把你的要求或反馈看得太个人化了。

sentences.en: You know, you'd say, I don't like it when you do that and they'd say, well, I guess I'm just a horrible mother.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你会说：“我不喜欢你那样做”，而他们会说：“好吧，我猜我只是个糟糕的母亲。”

sentences.en: I guess I'm the worst parent alive.
sentences.zh: “我猜我是活世上最糟糕的父母。”

sentences.en: That's a way of them basically saying, what you have to say doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是他们变相在说：你想说什么并不重要。

sentences.en: You have to protect my feelings.
sentences.zh: 你必须保护我的感受。

sentences.en: Emotionally immature parents are also very uncomfortable with vulnerability.
sentences.zh: 情绪不成熟的父母对脆弱也感到非常不舒服。

sentences.en: Kind of goes hand in hand with that last symptom.
sentences.zh: 这与上一个症状密切相关。

sentences.en: Often they may pretend to not hear you or understand you when you're sharing your feelings or they dismiss you.
sentences.zh: 当你分享自己的感受时，他们通常会假装听不见或听不懂，或者对你进行反驳和打发。

sentences.en: They say, can we talk about it later?
sentences.zh: 他们会说：“我们以后再谈这个好吗？”

sentences.en: They would maybe turn it back onto you or give you the silent treatment.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会把话题转回到你身上，或者对你进行冷暴力。

sentences.en: Any kind of emotional openness or vulnerability is really swept under the rug.
sentences.zh: 任何形式的情感敞开或脆弱都会被扫到地毯下面，置之不理。

sentences.en: They expect you to manage their emotions.
sentences.zh: 他们指望你来管理他们的情绪。

sentences.en: It's a very self-centered thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常以自我为中心的表现。

sentences.en: They make demands of you.
sentences.zh: 他们对你提出各种要求。

sentences.en: They ask you to essentially be their not just emotional witness but their psychologist, their counselor, their healer, their doctor, their marriage counselor.
sentences.zh: 他们本质上要求你不单单是他们的情感见证人，还要做他们的心理学家、顾问、治疗师、医生、婚姻调解人。

sentences.en: All these things that as a child, that's not your role.
sentences.zh: 所有这些作为一个孩子本不该扮演的角色。

sentences.en: It's not your role to parent them.
sentences.zh: 做他们的父母不是你的职责。

sentences.en: They are the adult.
sentences.zh: 他们才是成年人。

sentences.en: They are the ones who wanted you.
sentences.zh: 他们是想要孩子的人。

sentences.en: They are the ones who chose to have you and so they need to be, you know, ready to step into the role of parent and understand that it's not the same as being friends
sentences.zh: 他们是选择生下你的人，所以他们需要准备好承担父母的角色，明白这与和孩子做朋友

sentences.en: with your child.
sentences.zh: 是不一样的。

sentences.en: Being a parent and being a friend or being a counselor or being a partner, they're different things and as the child, you cannot be all of them.
sentences.zh: 做父母和做朋友、做顾问或做伴侣是不同的事情，作为孩子，你不可能把这些角色全包了。

sentences.en: That's something that they typically don't understand.
sentences.zh: 这是他们通常无法理解的一点。

sentences.en: It's very common when a parent will be like, oh yes, my daughter is like my best friend or my son is my best friend and that's always code for you guys
sentences.zh: 父母常说：“哦，是的，我女儿就像我最好的朋友”或者“我儿子是我最好的朋友”，这非常常见，这通常是暗指你们

sentences.en: don't have emotional boundaries.

sentences.zh: 因此，你也有能力掌控局面，为自己做出当下最好的选择，就像父母在你小时候本该为你做的那样，就像

sentences.zh: 他们现在本该为你做的那样。

sentences.en: The part of you, the childlike, innocent part of you who was injured by their behavior still exists and they still deserve love even if it was in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 你内心深处那个被他们的行为伤害过的、如孩子般天真的部分依然存在，他们依然值得被爱，哪怕这一切都已成为过去。

sentences.en: Re-parenting helps us heal that relationship with this past version of us and it helps us realize like, hey, it's not always going to be like this.
sentences.zh: 重新养育能帮助我们修复与过去自己的这种关系，并帮我们意识到，嘿，事情不会总是这样的。

sentences.en: There is an alternative.
sentences.zh: 还有别的选择。

sentences.en: There is a way that I deserve to be treated and I'm going to firstly begin by emulating it myself.
sentences.zh: 我值得被那样对待，而我首先要从自己开始模仿这种对待方式。

sentences.en: Now this might sound kind of intimidating at first but re-parenting really just means giving your adult self the grace and the security that your childhood self deserved.
sentences.zh: 这听起来一开始可能会有点吓人，但重新养育实际上只是意味着，给予你成年后的自己应得的宽容和安全感，这是你童年时就应得的。

sentences.en: So encouraging yourself when doubt creeps in, even when it feels unnatural.
sentences.zh: 所以在怀疑滋生时鼓励自己，哪怕这种感觉很不自然。

sentences.en: Holding yourself when you feel shame.
sentences.zh: 在感到羞耻时拥抱自己。

sentences.en: Allowing yourself to be playful.
sentences.zh: 允许自己保持顽皮。

sentences.en: Allowing yourself to be cringe.
sentences.zh: 允许自己显得幼稚或尴尬。

sentences.en: Allowing yourself to be vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 允许自己变得脆弱。

sentences.en: It could also be as simple as changing like your self-talk.
sentences.zh: 它也可以简单到改变你的自我对话方式。

sentences.en: So often, I just feel like we talk to ourselves so badly.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，我觉得我们对自己说话实在太恶劣了。

sentences.en: We say like, I'm so stupid.
sentences.zh: 我们会说，我太蠢了。

sentences.en: I'm a terrible person.
sentences.zh: 我是个糟糕的人。

sentences.en: I'm an idiot.
sentences.zh: 我是个白痴。

sentences.en: A lot of those words, we didn't learn those ourselves.
sentences.zh: 这些词汇中，有很多并不是我们自己想出来的。

sentences.en: They were words that were said to us.
sentences.zh: 而是别人曾经对我们说过的话。

sentences.en: And so replacing them and saying, I made a mistake and that's okay.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们要用这样的话来替换它们：我犯了个错误，这没关系。

sentences.en: I'm someone who was growing.
sentences.zh: 我是一个在成长的人。

sentences.en: I'm someone who was learning.
sentences.zh: 我是一个在学习的人。

sentences.en: That's essential because it's reprogramming our internal dialogue and the voice of our inner critic so that it is more gentle and understanding.
sentences.zh: 这至关重要，因为这正在重塑我们的内心独白和内心的批判声音，使其变得更加温和与包容。

sentences.en: You know, if you could go back to when you were, let's say, 5 or
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你能回到你比如说5岁、

sentences.en: 12 or 10 or 15, how would you wish your parents had responded to your emotional requests?
sentences.zh: 12岁、10岁或15岁的时候，你希望父母如何回应你的情感诉求？

sentences.en: How do you wish they had treated you?
sentences.zh: 你希望他们如何对待你？

sentences.en: How do you wish they had loved you?
sentences.zh: 你希望他们如何爱你？

sentences.en: Emulate that.
sentences.zh: 去模仿它。

sentences.en: Imagine it.
sentences.zh: 去想象它。

sentences.en: Deliver it back to yourself.
sentences.zh: 把它带回给自己。

sentences.en: Reparenting is also about noticing what you need right now over what others may need from you.
sentences.zh: 重新养育也是去关注你现在真正需要什么，而不是别人可能对你有什么需求。

sentences.en: If you have emotionally immature parents, you are most likely used to being very focused on their needs.
sentences.zh: 如果你的父母情感不成熟，你很可能已经习惯了高度关注他们的需求。

sentences.en: And that often ends up translating into other relationships as well.
sentences.zh: 而这种习惯往往最终也会带入到其他关系中。

sentences.en: That's not your job.
sentences.zh: 这不是你的工作。

sentences.en: Your job right now is to say, what do I need in this situation?
sentences.zh: 你现在的工作是去问：在这种情况下我需要什么？

sentences.en: What do I need at this point in my life?
sentences.zh: 在我人生的这个阶段我需要什么？

sentences.en: What do I need during my day?
sentences.zh: 在日常生活中我需要什么？

sentences.en: What do I need in a relationship?
sentences.zh: 在一段关系中我需要什么？

sentences.en: And going out, going after it and delivering it to yourself.
sentences.zh: 然后去行动，去追求它并满足自己。

sentences.en: The decisions that your parents never made for you, you can now make them.
sentences.zh: 父母以前从未为你做过的决定，你现在可以自己做了。

sentences.en: You can now decide, hey,
sentences.zh: 你现在可以决定，嘿，

sentences.en: I'm going to emotionally respond this way.
sentences.zh: 我要以这种方式来做出情感回应。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm going to have a nap at 2pm.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我下午2点要小睡一会儿。

sentences.en: Hey, I know that this relationship probably isn't right for me and
sentences.zh: 嘿，我知道这段关系可能并不适合我，

sentences.en: I'm going to walk away because I have agency.
sentences.zh: 我要离开，因为我有自主权。

sentences.en: And that's something that I think the children of emotionally immature parents often struggle with is this sense that like actually you are the boss and you are in charge
sentences.zh: 我认为情感不成熟父母的孩子往往很难接受这一点，他们很难摆脱这样一种感觉：实际上你才是老板，你才是在掌控全局的人，

sentences.en: and it's your life and it's your body and it's your emotions and your feelings and your reality.
sentences.zh: 这是你的人生，这是你的身体，这是你的情绪、你的感受和你的现实。

sentences.en: You can do what you want with that.
sentences.zh: 你可以随心所欲地处理这些。

sentences.en: You can make all of your choices from here on out and no matter how much of a fuss they kick up, whatever it is that they want to say, it doesn't change anything.
sentences.zh: 从今以后你可以做出所有的选择，不管他们闹出多大的动静，不管他们想说些什么，都无法改变任何事。

sentences.en: They don't control you.
sentences.zh: 他们无法控制你。

sentences.en: You are allowed to rewire what love feels like and say, I actually deserve more or I don't deserve this.
sentences.zh: 你有权重新定义爱的感觉，并告诉自己，其实我值得更好的，或者我不应该承受这些。

sentences.en: Okay, I'm getting very, you can say, I'm getting very passionate.
sentences.zh: 好了，我有点情绪激动，你可以说，我变得有点情绪化了。

sentences.en: So we're going to take a short break.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要稍微休息一下。

sentences.en: But when we return, we're going to talk through some of our listener questions.
sentences.zh: 但等我们回来后，我们将探讨一些听众提出的问题。

sentences.en: You guys had so many questions for me about emotionally immature parents in your own lives, in your partner's lives, in so many different ways.
sentences.zh: 你们向我提出了很多关于情感不成熟父母的问题，这些情况发生在你们自己的生活中、伴侣的生活中，以及形形色色的场景里。

sentences.en: There were so many questions and dilemmas that came up, so I'm excited to answer some of them.
sentences.zh: 有太多各种各样的问题和困境涌现出来，所以我很高兴能回答其中的一些。

sentences.en: Stay tuned.
sentences.zh: 请继续关注。

sentences.en: So you guys all know that each week I go on
sentences.zh: 所以你们都知道，每周我都会登录

sentences.en: Instagram at that psychology podcast if you want to follow and I tell you guys what I'm going to be talking about on this week's episode and I ask if you have any specific
sentences.zh: Instagram，账号是 that psychology podcast，如果你想关注的话。我会告诉大家我这期节目要聊什么主题，并询问大家是否有任何具体

sentences.en: questions you want answered.
sentences.zh: 的问题想要得到解答。

sentences.en: For some episodes like this one, the topic is so broad and our experiences like they are so different that I might not fully cover what you want to know.
sentences.zh: 对于某些像这样的一期节目，话题非常广泛，而且我们的经历又是如此不同，以至于我可能无法全面涵盖你想知道的内容。

sentences.en: Like I could do a six hour episode on this and still not touch on your unique specific circumstance.
sentences.zh: 比如我可以就这个主题做一个长达六小时的节目，却依然无法触及你那独一无二的具体境遇。

sentences.en: And so the listener questions are kind of the opportunity for me to touch on some of the more finer points.
sentences.zh: 因此，听众提问算是一个让我触及一些更细微要点的机会。

sentences.en: Let's start with question number one.
sentences.zh: 让我们从第一个问题开始。

sentences.en: What do you do when your parents put you in the middle of their fights?
sentences.zh: 当你的父母把你夹在他们的争吵中间时，你该怎么办？

sentences.en: This was by far the most common question, especially for people whose parents are getting divorced as they become adults or who have seen this happen for years and years and years
sentences.zh: 这绝对是最常见的问题，尤其是对那些父母在他们成年时正准备离婚的人，或者是多年来一直目睹这一切、

sentences.en: and are suddenly realizing like, hey, I'm the kid here.
sentences.zh: 然后突然意识到——嘿，我只是个孩子啊。

sentences.en: This actually shouldn't be my problem.
sentences.zh: 这其实根本不该是我的问题。

sentences.en: This is a classic example of parentification.
sentences.zh: 这是一个典型的“父母化”案例。

sentences.en: You have been put in the position of mediator, emotional regulator, diplomat.
sentences.zh: 你被推到了调解员、情感调节者、外交官的位置上。

sentences.en: You are parenting your parents when your role is meant to be as their child.
sentences.zh: 当你的角色本应是他们的孩子时，你却在反过来养育你的父母。

sentences.en: Let me say this.
sentences.zh: 请听我这么说。

sentences.en: This is not okay behavior from your parents.
sentences.zh: 父母有这种行为是绝对不对的。

sentences.en: You are not meant to be in the middle because you have a very different relationship with them compared to the relationship that they have with each other.
sentences.zh: 你不应该夹在中间，因为你跟他们的关系，和他们彼此之间的关系有着本质的不同。

sentences.en: And also, you are not a couple's counselor.
sentences.zh: 而且，你不是他们的婚姻心理咨询师。

sentences.en: You are not their best friend.
sentences.zh: 你不是他们的好朋友。

sentences.en: You are not the person they can rant to.
sentences.zh: 你不是他们可以倾倒苦水的人。

sentences.en: You are their child.
sentences.zh: 你是他们的孩子。

sentences.en: There are different relationships and we have different relationships with different people for a reason.
sentences.zh: 存在不同的关系，我们与不同的人建立不同的关系是有原因的。

sentences.en: Sometimes, though, the reason this happens is because A, they have no one else to talk about it to in their personal life, in which case they need to go and see a therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 然而有时，出现这种情况的原因是：A，他们在个人生活中找不到其他人来倾诉，这种情况下他们应该去看心理医生。

sentences.en: B, they feel like because you are so close to the situation, you can somehow be impartial, also incorrect.
sentences.zh: B，他们觉得因为你和这件事贴得足够近，所以你能做到某种程度的公正客观，这也是不对的。

sentences.en: C, sometimes it's just an accidental slip up.
sentences.zh: C，有时这只是一次无意的失言。

sentences.en: Or D, your opinion is actually becoming the battleground for them because you are the product of both of these two people.
sentences.zh: 或者D，你的意见实际上成了他们争夺的战场，因为你是这两个人共同的结晶。

sentences.en: So they may feel like, huh, if I can win you over, if you agree with me, well, then this other person has to listen.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能会觉得：哼，如果我能争取到你，如果你同意我的观点，那么另一个人就不得不听取意见。

sentences.en: You are the best weapon they could have in their arsenal.
sentences.zh: 你是他们武器库里能找到的最强武器。

sentences.en: The opinion of the child that the person and them both raise together.
sentences.zh: 也就是那个人和你共同抚养长大的孩子的意见。

sentences.en: So they win.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就赢了。

sentences.en: If they get you to agree with them, they win.
sentences.zh: 如果他们能让你同意他们的观点，他们就赢了。

sentences.en: It's very inappropriate.
sentences.zh: 这非常不合适。

sentences.en: It's also very uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 这也让人感到非常难受。

sentences.en: So I'm going to give you a sentence that you can use in these situations.
sentences.zh: 所以我将教你一句话，你可以在这种情况下使用。

sentences.en: That sounds really hard.
sentences.zh: 听起来真的很不容易。

sentences.en: But I'm not impartial here.
sentences.zh: 但我在这件事上无法做到公正。

sentences.en: And I really wish I could be, but it's just never going to happen.
sentences.zh: 我真的很希望自己能做到，但这注定是不可能的。

sentences.en: I really love mum slash dad, whoever it is, insert here.
sentences.zh: 我真的很爱妈妈/爸爸（无论具体是谁，在此填入）。

sentences.en: And I'm sure you value how much they love me and want me to stay close to both of you.
sentences.zh: 我也确信你很珍惜他们有多爱我，并且希望我能和你们俩都保持亲近。

sentences.en: So I can't be the person you vent to about that.
sentences.zh: 所以我无法成为那个让你倾诉这些烦恼的人。

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 真的很抱歉。

sentences.en: Short and simple.
sentences.zh: 简短而精炼。

sentences.en: And if they argue, play to their empathy.
sentences.zh: 如果他们争辩，就去唤起他们的同理心。

sentences.en: Ask them, how would you feel if you found out that mum slash dad was having these same conversations with me about you?
sentences.zh: 问问他们：如果有一天你发现妈妈/爸爸正在找你倾诉这些关于我的话题，你会怎么想？

sentences.en: Would you want that?
sentences.zh: 你会希望这样吗？

sentences.en: Probably not.
sentences.zh: 大概不会吧。

sentences.en: Or play dumb when they say, oh, you know, he just always does this or she's just like this and this and this.
sentences.zh: 或者当他们说，噢，你知道的，他总是这样，或者她就是这样这样这样时，装作一无所知。

sentences.en: Be like, oh, I'm, you know, I'm just a kid, really.
sentences.zh: 就好像，噢，你知道的，我其实只是个孩子。

sentences.en: Like, what would I know?
sentences.zh: 就像，我能懂什么？

sentences.en: Or, you know, I'm really young still.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道的，我还很年轻。

sentences.en: I don't really have much experience to know what you should do.
sentences.zh: 我其实没有什么经验来判断你应该怎么做。

sentences.en: I don't really understand this.
sentences.zh: 我其实不太懂这个。

sentences.en: Reinforce subliminally.
sentences.zh: 潜意识地进行强化。

sentences.en: Like, hey, hello.
sentences.zh: 比如，嘿，你好。

sentences.en: Reminder, I'm the child in this situation.
sentences.zh: 提醒一下，在这种情况下我才是孩子。

sentences.en: And I find that really, like, helpful to just just to be like almost give them a bit of a snap of the fingers, a wake up call.
sentences.zh: 我发现这样做真的很有帮助，就像是几乎给他们一个弹指，一个警钟。

sentences.en: Like, this isn't appropriate.
sentences.zh: 比如，这很不合适。

sentences.en: You know, it's inappropriate.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这不合时宜。

sentences.en: We're going to move on.
sentences.zh: 我们要说别的了。

sentences.en: Hopefully that kind of helps.
sentences.zh: 希望这能有所帮助。

sentences.en: Second question.
sentences.zh: 第二个问题。

sentences.en: I'm dating someone with immature parents, but they can't see it.
sentences.zh: 我在和父母不够成熟的人交往，但他们自己看不出来。

sentences.en: How can I firstly cope with it, but also help him to see that they have a problem?
sentences.zh: 我首先该如何应对，同时又该如何帮他意识到他们有问题？

sentences.en: This is a tough one.
sentences.zh: 这个问题很难处理。

sentences.en: I think firstly, you've got to realize that this is not something that you're going to be able to fix.
sentences.zh: 我想首先你得意识到，这不是你能解决的问题。

sentences.en: This is not a relationship that you can take charge of.
sentences.zh: 这不是一段你能由你来主导的关系。

sentences.en: This has most likely existed way before you came along.
sentences.zh: 这种情况多半在你出现之前很久就存在了。

sentences.en: You have to approach this really delicately.
sentences.zh: 你必须非常谨慎地处理这件事。

sentences.en: I always think about, like, trying to tell your friend that you hate their partner.
sentences.zh: 我总是会联想到，比如试图告诉朋友你讨厌他们的伴侣。

sentences.en: Nine out of ten times, they aren't going to see it the way that you do and they probably aren't going to listen and then you're just going to become the enemy.
sentences.zh: 十有八九，他们不会用你的视角来看待问题，也可能根本听不进去，最后你反而会变成敌人。

sentences.en: So please just remember as much as you want them to be happy and at peace and you want their life to be free of stress and tension, it's not your job to fix
sentences.zh: 所以请记住，尽管你希望他们幸福平静，希望他们的生活免受压力和紧张的困扰，但解决

sentences.en: their parents' relationship.
sentences.zh: 他们父母的关系并不是你的工作。

sentences.en: It's also not your job to make them see it and have to fix it either.
sentences.zh: 让他们看到这一点并不得不去解决，也不是你的工作。

sentences.en: You just want to try and slowly introduce the idea to them in a subtle way.
sentences.zh: 你只需要尝试以微妙的方式慢慢向他们引入这个想法。

sentences.en: So instead of being like, your parents are so immature, try something like, hey, have you ever noticed, like, this thing?
sentences.zh: 所以与其说“你的父母太不成熟了”，不如试着说“嘿，你有没有注意到这种事？”

sentences.en: How interesting.
sentences.zh: 多有意思啊。

sentences.en: Or how did you feel about that when they just did what they did just now, when they shut you down?
sentences.zh: 或者刚才他们做那些事、打断你的时候，你对此有什么感觉？

sentences.en: Or have you ever noticed that you kind of have to parent your parents emotionally?
sentences.zh: 或者你有没有注意到，你在情感上有点反过来照顾父母？

sentences.en: Oh, is that something that's been going on for a while?
sentences.zh: 噢，这种情况持续有一阵子了吗？

sentences.en: Like, oh, explain where that came from.
sentences.zh: 就像，噢，说说这事是怎么来的。

sentences.en: I want to know more about what it was like in your childhood.
sentences.zh: 我想更多地了解你童年时期的经历。

sentences.en: Like, these are very non-judgmental openings that let them discover patterns on their own.
sentences.zh: 看，这些都是非常不带评判色彩的切入点，能让他们自己发现规律。

sentences.en: And I really want you to remember, like, your role is to listen.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想让你记住，你的角色是倾听。

sentences.en: Your role is to really just
sentences.zh: 你的角色其实只是

sentences.en: facilitate them figuring it out for themselves and just to be open to that not always being linear.
sentences.zh: 协助他们自己想清楚，并且要接受这个过程不一定是一帆风顺的。

sentences.en: You know, they're not always going to be totally awake and open-eyed to the fact that their parents have some serious issues, like, from the moment that you start introducing
sentences.zh: 你知道的，从你开始引入这个概念的那一刻起，他们

sentences.en: the idea.
sentences.zh: 并不总是能立刻完全清醒并意识到他们的父母存在严重的问题。

sentences.en: And it might take them some time and there might be excuses.
sentences.zh: 这可能需要一些时间，而且可能会有各种借口。

sentences.en: But remember, you don't have to be around his family if you don't want to be.
sentences.zh: 但请记住，如果你不想的话，大可不必围着他的家人转。

sentences.en: If it comes up, that's when you can discuss it.
sentences.zh: 如果问题出现了，那正是你可以讨论的时候。

sentences.en: But this is going to sound controversial.
sentences.zh: 但这听起来可能会引发争议。
